title: Variance-Driven Cost Initiative — Sprint Catalyst for Adaptive Batching & Quant Profiles
creator: Amina Patel
description: Run a focused 6-week sprint to validate a variance-driven approach for applying batching, KV-prefetch, and quantization profiles. Rather than blanket policy changes, the initiative targets high-variance request cohorts and workloads with outsized token cost volatility. Deliver a validated playbook and a lightweight orchestration prototype that can: 1) detect high-variance cohorts from telemetry, 2) run controlled experiments with adaptive batching/quant profiles, and 3) produce rollout decision signals tied to cost and quality objectives. Out of scope: wholesale runtime kernel changes or hardware procurement. This ticket tracks the PM-level coordination, acceptance criteria, and experiment rubric.
goals: Reduce end-to-end token unit cost for identified high-variance cohorts by >= 12% without exceeding quality regression budget
Prove detection heuristic for variance cohorts with >70% precision and >60% recall over telemetry samples
Ship an experiment scaffolding template (Playbook + orchestration knobs) that SRE/Eng can reuse for follow-up pilots
metrics: primary_metric: median token-cost reduction on cohort (target >= 12%)
latency_slo: p99 request latency increase <= 10% vs baseline
quality_budget: BLEU/ROUGE/F1 proxies or evaluator-defined metrics, peak regression <= 2%
acceptance_criteria: Experiment template committed to repo with README and run instructions
Cohort detection algorithm evaluated on last 30 days of telemetry and meets precision/recall targets
At least two independent workloads show cost wins >= 12% under controlled A/B with quality within budget
Playbook and rollout decision checklist published to Confluence; stakeholders (SRE, Runtime, DX) signed off
notes_updates: 2025-05-01 Kickoff: aligned with Runtime, Observability, and SRE on scope; agreed to limit infra changes and focus on policy-layer experiments
2025-05-03 Hypothesis: variance-driven targeting will yield >2x ROI vs broad profile changes because it concentrates changes on tail-heavy cohorts
2025-05-07 Instrumentation: Observability added telemetry fields (per-route token variance, seq_len distribution) - PR: github.com/redwood/telemetry/pulls/412
2025-05-10 Experiment plan reviewed by Runtime: selected three candidate workloads (chat-widget, search-reorder, internal-assist) for pilot
2025-05-12 Early run: adaptive batching with small max batch (32->48) on cohort A showed 8% cost improvement but latency spike on 95th percentile; engineering proposed KV-prefetch gate to protect p95
2025-05-14 Decision: proceed with two parallel experiments (A: batching + KV gate, B: conservative quant profile + cache warmup). Added step to collect evaluator prompts for quality monitoring
2025-05-15 Blocker: Dedicated capacity quotas in eu-west-1 limit full-scale trials; mitigation: limit synthetic load and extend pilot window
risks_mitigations: Risk: quality regressions in subtle prompt classes - Mitigation: gated rollouts with automatic rollback if evaluator threshold crossed
Risk: infra capacity limits for parallel pilots - Mitigation: stagger trials and use synthetic generation with sampled traffic
Risk: detection false positives leading to needless changes - Mitigation: conservative detection threshold and manual review for first 30% of candidates
Risk: telemetry sampling bias - Mitigation: verify against raw request logs and run retrospective validation on full-day dumps
next_steps: Complete instrumentation PR review and deploy to staging (due 2025-05-18)
Kick off first controlled A/B for candidate workload A with SRE window (target start 2025-05-20)
Schedule mid-sprint review with Runtime and Observability (2025-05-27)
Publish initial playbook draft for internal review (2025-06-01)
